signals.name: No Access Management System
signals.description: Access to system components is not managed systematically.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Identity and access management systems User directories and authentication services Administrative access to CDE components Remote access to payment systems

related_controls: 7.3 Access to system components and data is managed via an access control system(s).
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Assess whether an access control system is deployed to manage user permissions across system components. Look for centralized identity management platforms, directory services, or access governance tools. Manual or decentralized access management without systematic controls indicates this signal.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 7: Restrict Access to System Components

signals.name: No Access Restriction Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for restricting access based on business need to know.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Identity and access management systems User directories and authentication services Administrative access to CDE components Remote access to payment systems

related_controls: 7.1 Processes and mechanisms for restricting access to system components and cardholder data by business need to know are defined and understood.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review organizational policies and procedures for evidence of documented access restriction processes. Look for formal access request and approval workflows, documented business justification requirements, and periodic access reviews. Absence of these documented processes indicates this signal.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 7: Restrict Access to System Components

signals.name: No Role-Based Access Control
signals.description: Access to system components is not appropriately defined based on roles.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Identity and access management systems User directories and authentication services Administrative access to CDE components Remote access to payment systems

related_controls: 7.2 Access to system components and data is appropriately defined and assigned.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Examine user account configurations and permissions to determine if access is granted based on defined roles or assigned ad-hoc. Review access control models for evidence of role definitions, privilege mappings, and least privilege principles. Missing or undefined role-based access structures indicate this signal.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 7: Restrict Access to System Components

signals.name: No Authentication Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for user identification and authentication.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Identity and access management systems User directories and authentication services Administrative access to CDE components Remote access to payment systems

related_controls: 8.1 Processes and mechanisms for identifying and authenticating users are defined and understood.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review documentation for formal authentication and identification processes. Look for defined user provisioning workflows, authentication method standards, and account lifecycle management procedures. Absence of documented processes for managing user identities and authentication indicates this signal.

signals.name: No Authenticator Management
signals.description: Accounts and authentication factors are not strictly managed.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Identity and access management systems User directories and authentication services Administrative access to CDE components Remote access to payment systems

related_controls: 8.6 Use of application and system accounts and associated authentication factors is strictly managed.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review system and application account management practices. Look for controls preventing interactive login to service accounts, monitoring of authentication factor usage, and documentation of exceptional access. Uncontrolled service accounts, missing authentication factor management, or lack of accountability for privileged account usage indicates this signal.

signals.name: No User ID Lifecycle Management
signals.description: User and administrator IDs are not managed throughout the account lifecycle.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Identity and access management systems User directories and authentication services Administrative access to CDE components Remote access to payment systems

related_controls: 8.2 User identification and related accounts for users and administrators are strictly managed throughout an account's lifecycle.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Examine user account provisioning and deprovisioning processes. Look for evidence of unique user ID assignments, proper account creation procedures, timely account disablement upon termination, and regular account reviews. Shared accounts, missing deprovisioning processes, or lack of account lifecycle tracking indicates this signal.

signals.name: No Multi-Factor Authentication
signals.description: Multi-factor authentication is not used to secure CDE access.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Identity and access management systems User directories and authentication services Administrative access to CDE components Remote access to payment systems

related_controls: 8.4 Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is implemented to secure access into the CDE.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review authentication mechanisms for CDE access points including administrative consoles, remote access solutions, and application interfaces. Verify that at least two independent authentication factors (something you know, something you have, something you are) are required. Single-factor authentication to CDE components indicates this signal.

signals.name: No Secure MFA Configuration
signals.description: MFA systems are not configured securely to prevent misuse.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Identity and access management systems User directories and authentication services Administrative access to CDE components Remote access to payment systems

related_controls: 8.5 Multi-factor authentication (MFA) systems are configured to prevent misuse.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Test MFA implementations for security weaknesses including replay attack vulnerabilities, bypass mechanisms, and configuration flaws. Review MFA system settings for replay protection, session management, and bypass prevention controls. Vulnerable or bypassable MFA configurations indicate this signal.

signals.name: No Strong Authentication
signals.description: Strong authentication is not established (passwords less than 12 characters, no complexity).
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Identity and access management systems User directories and authentication services Administrative access to CDE components Remote access to payment systems

related_controls: 8.3 Strong authentication for users and administrators is established and managed.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Analyze password policies and authentication configurations. Check minimum password length requirements, complexity rules (numeric, alphabetic, special characters), and enforcement mechanisms. Passwords shorter than 12 characters or lacking complexity requirements indicate this signal.

signals.name: No Secure Configuration Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for applying secure configurations to system components.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Point-of-sale (POS) systems Network infrastructure within CDE scope

related_controls: 2.1 Processes and mechanisms for applying secure configurations to all system components are defined and understood.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for missing secure configuration standards, lack of hardening procedures for different system types, absence of documented baseline configurations, missing change management processes for security configurations, and no defined responsibilities for maintaining secure configurations across the environment.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 2: Apply Secure Configurations

signals.name: No Secure System Configuration
signals.description: System components are not securely configured (default passwords not changed, unnecessary services enabled).
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Point-of-sale (POS) systems Network infrastructure within CDE scope

related_controls: 2.2 System components are configured and managed securely.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Scan for default credentials and accounts, identify unnecessary services and protocols running on systems, check for missing security patches and hardening measures, verify that configuration standards align with industry best practices (CIS benchmarks, vendor hardening guides), and assess whether single-function servers are properly segregated by security level.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 2: Apply Secure Configurations

signals.name: No Wireless Security Configuration
signals.description: Wireless environments are not securely configured and managed.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Point-of-sale (POS) systems Network infrastructure within CDE scope

related_controls: 2.3 Wireless environments are configured and managed securely.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Identify wireless access points with default credentials or SSIDs, check for weak encryption protocols (WEP, WPA), verify wireless networks are properly isolated from CDE, assess whether rogue access points are being detected, and examine wireless authentication mechanisms for compliance with current security standards (WPA2/WPA3 with strong encryption).

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 2: Apply Secure Configurations

signals.name: No Audit Logs
signals.description: Audit logs are not implemented for threat detection and forensic analysis.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 10.2 Audit logs are implemented to support the detection of anomalies and suspicious activity, and the forensic analysis of events
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for disabled logging on CDE systems, absence of audit trail generation, missing log data for critical events (authentication, access, changes), or evidence of insufficient logging coverage for security-relevant activities.

signals.name: No Security Failure Detection
signals.description: Failures of security systems are not detected, reported, or responded to.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 10.7 Failures of critical security control systems are detected, reported, and responded to promptly
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for absence of security system health monitoring, lack of alerting for security control failures (firewall, IDS/IPS, logging system failures), missing incident response procedures for security system outages, or evidence of undetected/unreported failures in critical security controls.

signals.name: No Log Protection
signals.description: Audit logs are not protected from unauthorized modification or deletion.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 10.3 Audit logs are protected from destruction and unauthorized modifications
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for world-writable log files, lack of log file integrity monitoring, missing access controls on log directories, absence of centralized logging, or evidence of log tampering or deletion capabilities by unauthorized users.

signals.name: No Log Retention
signals.description: Audit log history is not retained (3 months immediately available, 1 year archived).
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 10.5 Audit log history is retained and available for analysis
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for log rotation policies that delete logs too soon, absence of log archival systems, insufficient storage capacity for log retention, missing backup of historical logs, or evidence of logs being retained for less than the required 12-month period.

signals.name: No Log Review
signals.description: Audit logs are not reviewed to identify suspicious activity.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 10.4 Audit logs are reviewed to identify anomalies or suspicious activity
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for absence of log review procedures, lack of documented review activities, missing SIEM alerts or monitoring, no evidence of daily log analysis, or outdated/unreviewed security event logs.

signals.name: No Logging Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for logging and monitoring access.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 10.1 Processes and mechanisms for logging and monitoring all access to system components and cardholder data are defined and documented
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for absence of logging policies, lack of documented logging procedures, missing log management processes, or evidence of undefined audit trail requirements for CDE systems.

signals.name: No Time Synchronization
signals.description: Time synchronization is not implemented for consistent log timestamps.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 10.6 Time synchronization mechanisms support consistent time settings across all systems
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for missing NTP configuration, systems with inconsistent time settings, absence of authoritative time sources, disabled time sync services, or evidence of significant clock drift across CDE systems that would compromise log correlation.

signals.name: No Anti-Phishing Mechanisms
signals.description: No anti-phishing mechanisms to protect users from phishing attacks.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment application developers E-commerce platforms and merchants Systems and endpoints within CDE scope Web applications handling payment data

related_controls: 5.4 - Suspected and confirmed security incidents that are identified are responded to immediately
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Check for absence of email security controls such as SPF, DKIM, and DMARC validation. Monitor for lack of URL filtering, link rewriting, or sandboxing capabilities. Identify missing browser-based phishing protection features. Review security awareness training gaps related to phishing recognition. Detect environments without phishing simulation or testing programs to validate user awareness and technical controls.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 5: Protect All Systems and Networks from Malicious Software

signals.name: No Malware Detection/Prevention
signals.description: Malicious software is not detected, prevented, or addressed.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment application developers E-commerce platforms and merchants Systems and endpoints within CDE scope Web applications handling payment data

related_controls: 5.2 - Malicious software (malware) is prevented, or detected and addressed
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Identify systems and endpoints lacking anti-malware software deployment. Monitor for disabled or non-functional anti-malware solutions. Check for systems excluded from anti-malware requirements without proper risk assessments. Review endpoint security inventory against deployed anti-malware coverage. Detect malware infections that were not prevented or blocked by security controls, indicating gaps in protection mechanisms.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 5: Protect All Systems and Networks from Malicious Software

signals.name: No Anti-Malware Monitoring
signals.description: Anti-malware mechanisms are not actively monitored.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment application developers E-commerce platforms and merchants Systems and endpoints within CDE scope Web applications handling payment data

related_controls: 5.3 - Anti-malware mechanisms and processes are active, maintained, and monitored
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor for anti-malware solutions with outdated signatures or definitions. Detect disabled automatic updates or scan schedules. Check for anti-malware logs that are not being collected, retained, or reviewed. Identify systems where anti-malware software is installed but not actively running or scanning. Review monitoring dashboards for gaps in anti-malware status visibility and alerting mechanisms.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 5: Protect All Systems and Networks from Malicious Software

signals.name: No Malware Protection Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for protecting against malicious software.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment application developers E-commerce platforms and merchants Systems and endpoints within CDE scope Web applications handling payment data

related_controls: 5.1 - Processes and mechanisms for protecting all systems and networks from malicious software are defined and understood
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor for absence of documented malware protection policies, procedures, and processes. Review policy repositories, documentation systems, and security program artifacts. Look for gaps in malware protection lifecycle documentation including prevention, detection, response, and recovery procedures. Verify that anti-malware program governance structures and responsibilities are clearly defined and communicated.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 5: Protect All Systems and Networks from Malicious Software

signals.name: No CDE Access Restriction
signals.description: Access to the Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) is not properly restricted.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Point-of-sale (POS) systems Network infrastructure within CDE scope

related_controls: 1.3 Network access to and from the cardholder data environment is restricted.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Identify unrestricted network paths to CDE, check for missing network segmentation controls, verify wireless network isolation from CDE, examine whether direct Internet access from CDE is properly controlled, and assess if internal networks have unrestricted access to CDE components.

signals.name: No Network Connection Control
signals.description: Network connections between trusted and untrusted networks are not controlled.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Point-of-sale (POS) systems Network infrastructure within CDE scope

related_controls: 1.4 Network connections between trusted and untrusted networks are controlled.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Check for missing controls at trust boundaries, verify anti-spoofing measures (such as RFC 1918 filtering), examine whether public-facing systems can directly access CDE, assess controls on VPN and remote access connections, and review filtering of internal IP addresses at external network boundaries.

signals.name: No Network Security Control Configuration
signals.description: Network Security Controls (NSC) such as firewalls, virtual devices, and cloud access controls are not properly configured and managed.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Point-of-sale (POS) systems Network infrastructure within CDE scope

related_controls: 1.2 Network security controls (NSCs) are configured and maintained.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review firewall configurations for default-allow rules, check for undocumented rules, verify NSCs are installed at all network boundaries, examine cloud security group configurations, and assess whether all inbound/outbound traffic to CDE is explicitly authorized and documented.

signals.name: No Network Security Control Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for maintaining network security controls.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Point-of-sale (POS) systems Network infrastructure within CDE scope

related_controls: 1.1 Processes and mechanisms for installing and maintaining network security controls are defined and understood.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for missing or outdated network security policies, lack of documented procedures for firewall rule management, absence of network diagrams showing CDE boundaries, and missing processes for reviewing and approving network configuration changes.

signals.name: No Untrusted Network Risk Mitigation
signals.description: Risks from untrusted networks (including the Internet) are not mitigated.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Point-of-sale (POS) systems Network infrastructure within CDE scope

related_controls: 1.5 Risks to the CDE from computing devices that are able to connect to both untrusted networks and the CDE are mitigated.
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Identify dual-homed systems without proper controls, check for missing endpoint protection on devices accessing CDE, verify presence of personal firewall software on portable devices, assess controls for BYOD and contractor devices, and examine whether split-tunneling is properly controlled on VPN connections to CDE.

signals.name: No Physical Access Controls
signals.description: Physical access controls do not mediate entry into areas containing cardholder data.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 9.2 Physical access controls manage entry into facilities and systems containing cardholder data
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for missing badge readers, lack of access control systems, absence of physical barriers, uncontrolled entry points to CDE areas, or evidence of unrestricted physical access to sensitive systems.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 9: Restrict Physical Access

signals.name: No Physical Access Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for physically restricting access to the CDE.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 9.1 Processes and mechanisms for restricting physical access to cardholder data are defined and understood
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for absence of documented physical security policies, lack of defined processes for CDE access control, missing physical security procedures, or absence of physical access restriction mechanisms in policy documentation.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 9: Restrict Physical Access

signals.name: No Media Security
signals.description: Media containing cardholder data is not stored, accessed, and destroyed securely.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 9.4 Media with cardholder data is securely stored, accessed, transported, and destroyed
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for unsecured backup tapes, unencrypted removable media, lack of media inventory tracking, absence of secure destruction processes, or evidence of improper media handling and disposal procedures.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 9: Restrict Physical Access

signals.name: No POI Device Protection
signals.description: Point of interaction (POI) devices are not protected from tampering and substitution.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 9.5 Point of interaction (POI) devices are protected from tampering and unauthorized substitution
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for absence of device inventory lists, lack of tamper-evident seals, missing device inspection procedures, no tracking of POI device serial numbers, or evidence of unmonitored payment terminals vulnerable to skimming attacks.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 9: Restrict Physical Access

signals.name: No Visitor Management
signals.description: Physical access for visitors and personnel is not authorized and managed.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Data centers and server rooms housing CDE Point-of-sale (POS) environments Payment terminal locations SIEM and log management systems All systems within CDE scope

related_controls: 9.3 Physical access for personnel and visitors is authorized and managed
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Look for absence of visitor logs, lack of escort procedures, missing visitor badge systems, no authorization process for CDE access, or evidence of unmanaged visitor access to sensitive areas.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 9: Restrict Physical Access

signals.name: No Acceptable Use Policy
signals.description: No acceptable use policies for critical technologies.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 12.2 - Acceptable use policies for end-user technologies are defined and implemented
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Verify existence of acceptable use policies covering end-user technologies such as remote access, wireless, removable media, laptops, tablets, handheld devices, email, and internet usage. Monitor for employee acknowledgment and periodic review of policies.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 12: Support Information Security with Organizational Policies

signals.name: No Annual Policy Review
signals.description: Security policies are not reviewed at least annually.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 12.1 - A comprehensive information security policy that governs and provides direction for protection of the entity's information assets is known and current
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor for absence of annual policy review documentation, including review dates, participants, changes made, and approval signatures. Verify that all security policies and procedures are reviewed annually and updated to reflect environmental or business changes. Check for policy version control and distribution tracking.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 12: Support Information Security with Organizational Policies

signals.name: No Compliance Management
signals.description: No processes for managing ongoing PCI DSS compliance.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 12.4 - PCI DSS compliance is managed
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: For service providers, verify executive-level responsibility for PCI DSS compliance and documented compliance program charter. For all entities, monitor for compliance tracking mechanisms, quarterly and annual assessment schedules, and remediation management processes.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 12: Support Information Security with Organizational Policies

signals.name: No Incident Response Plan
signals.description: No incident response plan for security incidents affecting the CDE.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 12.10 - Suspected and confirmed security incidents that could impact the cardholder data environment are responded to immediately
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Verify existence of documented incident response plan covering detection, containment, analysis, recovery, and post-incident activities. Monitor for annual plan reviews, testing exercises, incident response team training, and 24/7 incident response availability. Check for incident logging and evidence retention procedures.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 12: Support Information Security with Organizational Policies

signals.name: No Personnel Screening
signals.description: Personnel are not screened to minimize insider threat risk.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 12.7 - Personnel are screened to reduce risks from insider threats
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Verify existence of pre-employment screening procedures for personnel with CDE access, including background checks, reference checks, and identity verification. Monitor HR records for screening completion and compliance with local laws. Check for screening of contractors and third-party personnel.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 12: Support Information Security with Organizational Policies

signals.name: No Risk Assessment
signals.description: Risks to the CDE are not formally identified, evaluated, and managed.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 12.3 - Risks to the cardholder data environment are formally identified, evaluated, and managed
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Check for documented risk assessment methodology and recent risk assessment reports covering the CDE. Verify annual risk assessments and assessments after significant changes. Monitor for risk treatment plans and evidence of risk-based decision making.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 12: Support Information Security with Organizational Policies

signals.name: No PCI DSS Scope Documentation
signals.description: PCI DSS scope is not documented and validated.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 12.5 - PCI DSS scope is documented and validated
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Verify existence of current system inventory documenting all in-scope components, network diagrams showing CDE boundaries, data flow diagrams, and annual scope validation documentation. Monitor for scope changes and corresponding documentation updates.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 12: Support Information Security with Organizational Policies

signals.name: No Information Security Policy
signals.description: No comprehensive information security policy maintained and kept current.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 12.1 - A comprehensive information security policy that governs and provides direction for protection of the entity's information assets is known and current
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor for the absence of a documented, board-approved information security policy. Verify that the policy addresses all PCI DSS requirements, is reviewed annually, and is distributed to all affected personnel. Check for policy version control and acknowledgment tracking.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 12: Support Information Security with Organizational Policies

signals.name: No Security Awareness Training
signals.description: No annual security awareness training for employees.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 12.6 - Security awareness education is an ongoing activity
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor for absence of documented security awareness program, training materials, attendance records, and acknowledgment forms. Verify annual training completion for all personnel with access to cardholder data or the CDE. Check for training content covering security policies, acceptable use, and incident reporting.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 12: Support Information Security with Organizational Policies

signals.name: No TPSP Compliance Support
signals.description: Third-party service providers do not support customers' PCI compliance.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 12.9 - Third-party service providers (TPSPs) support their customers' PCI DSS compliance
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: For service providers, verify written acknowledgments to customers regarding data security responsibilities, documentation of services provided, and evidence of PCI DSS compliance status communication. Monitor for customer-facing compliance documentation and support processes.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 12: Support Information Security with Organizational Policies

signals.name: No Third-Party Service Provider Management
signals.description: Third-party service provider risks are not managed.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 12.8 - Risk to information assets associated with third-party service provider (TPSP) relationships is managed
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Verify existence of TPSP inventory, due diligence procedures, written agreements addressing data security responsibilities, and ongoing monitoring processes. Monitor for PCI DSS compliance status tracking of TPSPs and evidence of annual reviews.

sources.title: PCI DSS v4.0
sources.section: Requirement 12: Support Information Security with Organizational Policies

signals.name: No Secure Change Management
signals.description: Changes to applications and software are not managed securely.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment application developers E-commerce platforms and merchants Systems and endpoints within CDE scope Web applications handling payment data

related_controls: 6.5 - Changes to all system components are managed securely
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor for unauthorized changes to production systems and applications. Review change management tickets for missing security impact assessments or approvals. Detect deployments that bypass established change control processes (shadow IT, emergency changes without proper documentation). Check for inadequate separation between development, testing, and production environments. Identify changes deployed without adequate testing, security validation, or rollback procedures. Review configuration management databases for drift between documented and actual system states.

signals.name: No Secure Coding Practices
signals.description: Custom software is not developed using secure coding practices.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment application developers E-commerce platforms and merchants Systems and endpoints within CDE scope Web applications handling payment data

related_controls: 6.2 - Bespoke and custom software are developed securely
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review code repositories for lack of secure coding standards compliance. Detect common vulnerabilities such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), insecure authentication, or hardcoded credentials in source code. Monitor for absence of code review processes or automated security scanning tools. Check for developer training gaps in secure coding techniques. Identify custom applications developed without following OWASP or similar security guidelines.

signals.name: No Secure Development Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for developing secure systems and software.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment application developers E-commerce platforms and merchants Systems and endpoints within CDE scope Web applications handling payment data

related_controls: 6.1 - Processes and mechanisms for developing and maintaining secure systems and software are defined and understood
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor for absence of secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) documentation and procedures. Review development processes for lack of security requirements, design reviews, or security testing phases. Check for missing secure coding standards, guidelines, or training materials. Identify gaps in development environment security controls and separation of duties. Verify that security activities are integrated throughout the development lifecycle rather than added as an afterthought.

signals.name: No Vulnerability Management
signals.description: Software vulnerabilities are not identified and addressed through patching.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment application developers E-commerce platforms and merchants Systems and endpoints within CDE scope Web applications handling payment data

related_controls: 6.3 - Security vulnerabilities are identified and addressed
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor vulnerability scanning results for unpatched systems and applications. Identify systems with outdated software versions or missing critical security patches. Review patch management processes for gaps in vulnerability assessment, prioritization, or remediation timelines. Detect systems excluded from vulnerability scanning without proper justification. Check for absence of vulnerability disclosure monitoring or threat intelligence feeds to identify new vulnerabilities affecting deployed software.

signals.name: No Web Application Protection
signals.description: Public-facing web applications are not protected against attacks.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment application developers E-commerce platforms and merchants Systems and endpoints within CDE scope Web applications handling payment data

related_controls: 6.4 - Public-facing web applications are protected against attacks
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Identify public-facing web applications without Web Application Firewall (WAF) protection or equivalent automated security controls. Monitor for WAFs in detection-only mode without active blocking capabilities. Check for outdated WAF rulesets or missing OWASP Top 10 coverage. Review web application security testing results for vulnerabilities that should be mitigated by protective controls. Detect gaps in web application layer logging and monitoring that would prevent attack detection.

signals.name: No Account Data Minimization
signals.description: Account data in storage exceeds the minimum necessary for business operations.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Database systems containing payment card data Data transmission channels and APIs

related_controls: 3.2 Account data storage is kept to a minimum
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Audit data storage repositories to identify cardholder data that exceeds business justification. Review data retention policies and verify implementation. Check for excessive storage duration, unnecessary data fields, or redundant copies of cardholder data. Examine database schemas and storage systems for compliance with data minimization principles.

signals.name: No Stored Data Protection Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for protecting stored account data.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Database systems containing payment card data Data transmission channels and APIs

related_controls: 3.1 Processes and mechanisms for protecting stored account data are defined and understood
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review organizational documentation for data protection policies and procedures. Check for absence of documented processes covering data storage security, retention policies, and protection mechanisms. Verify whether security controls for stored cardholder data are documented and understood by personnel handling payment card information.

signals.name: No Key Management Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for securely managing cryptographic keys.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Database systems containing payment card data Data transmission channels and APIs

related_controls: 3.7 Where cryptography is used to protect stored account data, key management processes and procedures are defined and implemented
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review documentation for key management lifecycle processes including generation, distribution, storage, change/rotation, retirement, and destruction. Verify existence of procedures for key custodian responsibilities, split knowledge, dual control, and periodic key changes. Check for documented processes covering compromised key handling, key strength requirements, and secure key distribution methods. Assess implementation of cryptoperiod policies and key archival procedures.

signals.name: No Cryptographic Key Security
signals.description: Cryptographic keys used to protect account data are not adequately secured.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Database systems containing payment card data Data transmission channels and APIs

related_controls: 3.6 Cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data are secured
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review key storage mechanisms for proper protection including encryption of data-encrypting keys with key-encrypting keys. Verify keys are not stored in clear text or in the same location as encrypted data. Check access controls limiting key access to custodians. Audit key storage locations including hardware security modules (HSMs), key management systems, and secure cryptographic devices. Assess split knowledge and dual control implementations.

signals.name: No PAN View/Copy Access Control
signals.description: No restrictions on view and copy access to Primary Account Numbers (PAN).
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Database systems containing payment card data Data transmission channels and APIs

related_controls: 3.4 Access to displays of full PAN and ability to copy PAN is restricted
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review access control configurations for applications, databases, and systems displaying PANs. Verify implementation of masking or truncation for users without legitimate business need. Test copy/paste functionality and screen capture controls. Audit user roles and permissions to ensure least privilege. Check for unmasked PANs in user interfaces, reports, and logs.

signals.name: No PAN Storage Protection
signals.description: PANs are not rendered unreadable everywhere they are stored (encryption, truncation, hashing).
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Database systems containing payment card data Data transmission channels and APIs

related_controls: 3.5 Primary account number is secured wherever it is stored
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Scan all storage locations for unencrypted or plaintext PANs, including databases, file systems, removable media, backups, and logs. Verify encryption implementation meets PCI DSS standards for cryptographic strength. Check for proper truncation (maximum first 6 and last 4 digits). Review tokenization systems and hash implementations. Test data protection across all storage environments including cloud, on-premises, and portable media.

signals.name: Sensitive Authentication Data Retained
signals.description: Sensitive authentication data (full track data, CVV, PIN) is stored after authorization.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Database systems containing payment card data Data transmission channels and APIs

related_controls: 3.3 Sensitive authentication data is not stored after authorization
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Scan databases, log files, and storage systems for prohibited sensitive authentication data elements. Check for full magnetic stripe data (tracks 1, 2, or equivalent chip data), CVV2/CVC2/CID values, and PIN/PIN block data. Review application code and data flows to identify improper retention. Monitor backup systems and archived data for SAD presence post-authorization.

signals.name: No Intrusion Detection/Prevention
signals.description: No intrusion detection/prevention systems to detect unauthorized network activity.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 11.5 - Network intrusions and unexpected file changes are detected and responded to
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Verify deployment of IDS/IPS solutions at the CDE perimeter and critical internal points. Monitor for active alerting mechanisms, signature updates, and response procedures. Check for continuous monitoring coverage and alert review processes.

signals.name: No Payment Page Change Detection
signals.description: Changes to payment pages are not detected for tamper prevention.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 11.6 - Unauthorized changes on payment pages are detected and responded to
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor for file integrity monitoring (FIM) or change detection mechanisms on payment pages and scripts. Verify automated alerts for unauthorized modifications to payment forms, JavaScript, and related content. Check for regular reviews of payment page integrity and incident response procedures for detected changes.

signals.name: No Penetration Testing
signals.description: Penetration tests are not performed at least annually.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 11.4 - External and internal penetration testing is regularly performed, and exploitable vulnerabilities and security weaknesses are corrected
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Verify existence of annual penetration testing reports covering network-layer and application-layer testing. Check for testing performed by qualified internal resources or external third parties. Monitor for tests after significant infrastructure or application upgrades.

signals.name: No Security Testing Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for network security testing.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 11.1 - Processes and mechanisms for regularly testing security of systems and networks are defined and understood
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor for the absence of documented security testing processes, procedures, and schedules. Verify that testing processes are defined for all network components and security controls within the cardholder data environment (CDE).

signals.name: No Vulnerability Scanning
signals.description: Internal and external vulnerability scans are not performed quarterly.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 11.3 - External and internal vulnerabilities are regularly identified, prioritized, and addressed
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor for absence of quarterly vulnerability scan reports from an Approved Scanning Vendor (ASV) for external scans and internal scanning tools. Verify scan schedules, coverage of all system components in the CDE, and remediation tracking for identified vulnerabilities.

signals.name: No Wireless AP Detection
signals.description: Wireless access points are not monitored for unauthorized devices.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Security and compliance teams Human resources and training departments Third-party service providers (TPSPs) Incident response teams

related_controls: 11.2 - Wireless access points are identified and monitored, and unauthorized wireless access points are addressed
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Check for automated wireless detection systems or manual testing procedures. Verify that wireless scans are conducted at least quarterly and after significant changes. Alert on absence of wireless detection logs or tools.

signals.name: No Transmission Encryption Processes
signals.description: No defined processes for encrypting cardholder data during transmission.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Database systems containing payment card data Data transmission channels and APIs

related_controls: 4.1 Processes and mechanisms for protecting cardholder data with strong cryptography during transmission over open, public networks are defined and understood
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review organizational documentation for transmission security policies and procedures. Check for absence of documented processes covering encryption protocols, cipher suites, certificate management, and secure transmission requirements. Verify whether security controls for data in transit are documented and understood by personnel responsible for network security and data transmission systems.

signals.name: No PAN Transmission Encryption
signals.description: PANs are not protected with strong cryptography during transmission over public networks.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Organizations processing, storing, or transmitting cardholder data Payment processors and service providers E-commerce platforms and merchants Database systems containing payment card data Data transmission channels and APIs

related_controls: 4.2 PAN is protected with strong cryptography whenever it is sent over open, public networks
metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Monitor network traffic for unencrypted PAN transmissions over public networks including the Internet, wireless networks, and cellular technologies. Verify implementation of TLS 1.2 or higher with strong cipher suites. Check for weak protocols (SSL, early TLS versions) and insecure fallback mechanisms. Review certificate validation processes and trust store configurations. Test end-to-end encryption for payment transactions, APIs, and data exchanges.
